S8.01.needs: a conversation with a message you sent
S8.01.note: The Save & Retry button uses variant default (packages/ui/ui/src/primitives/Button.tsx:13). Label contrast was not measured.
steps: Sign in and open a conversation that has a message you sent.
Hover your sent message and click the pencil icon (Edit message).
Change the text in the edit box.
Look at the Save & Retry button: it should look like the emphasised main action, with readable label text, compared with Cancel.
S8.01.where: Chat > hover one of your sent messages > Edit message (pencil icon) > Save & Retry

S8.02.note: Copy is an outline button (ShareConversationDialog.tsx:304). The code does not show a filled primary button beside it in this dialog, so the pairing is not confirmed.
steps: Open a conversation and open its title menu.
Click Share….
Create a link if the dialog asks, then look at the Copy button beside the Conversation link box.
Compare: Copy should look like a lighter outline button, not the filled primary style.
S8.02.where: Chat > conversation title menu > Share… > Copy (next to the Conversation link box)

S8.03.needs: a shared conversation whose link list is incomplete (hard to create by hand)
S8.03.note: The button shows only when inventoryIncomplete is true and no link is active (ShareConversationDialog.tsx:414-417). Do not click it to test; it revokes links.
steps: Open a conversation title menu and click Share….
Look for the Revoke every link button in the dialog footer.
If it is missing, the link list is complete, so the button is not shown; note that.
If it appears, hover and compare its red danger colour with the other buttons.
S8.03.where: Chat > conversation title menu > Share… > Revoke every link (red button, shown only when the link list is incomplete and no link is active)

S8.04.needs: a conversation with a message you sent
S8.04.note: The accessible names Retry this message and Edit message are not visible words; they are aria-labels.
steps: Sign in and open a conversation with a message you sent.
Hover the sent message so the action icons appear.
Hover the icon buttons to see the tooltips Retry and Edit.
Check that each icon button has a name for screen readers (aria-label Retry this message and Edit message) using a screen reader or accessibility inspector.
S8.04.where: Chat > hover one of your sent messages > the icon-only Retry and Edit buttons (tooltips Retry and Edit)

S8.06.note: The + button uses aria-pressed and aria-expanded (ChatComposerNew.tsx:5977-5978). The label is an aria-label, not visible text.
steps: Open a chat and find the + button beside the message box.
Click it and see whether a menu opens.
If a tool or attachment is active, check that the + button shows a count badge.
Look at the button's pressed state in an accessibility inspector: it should expose aria-pressed and aria-expanded.
S8.06.where: Chat > the + button at the left of the message box (Add attachments and tools)

S8.07.note: The start-dictation control's visible text was not found in the code; the grouping labels are aria-labels.
steps: Open a chat and start voice dictation from the composer.
Look at the strip that appears above the message box.
Hover or focus the round X button to see its name Discard recording.
Compare the grouped controls with the group name Voice dictation in an accessibility inspector.
S8.07.where: Chat > composer > start voice dictation > the Voice dictation strip with its Discard recording button

S8.08.needs: a Free account or a paid account; an internet connection
S8.08.note: Link styling and rendering were found in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/MarkdownContent.tsx; the exact styling values were not checked.
steps: Send a message that asks for a reply with a web link, such as a website address.
Find a link in the reply.
Check it is styled as a link (coloured, underlined or otherwise marked).
Click it and see that it opens its destination.
S8.08.where: Chat > any assistant reply that contains a web link

S8.09.note: The Create project button that opens the dialog was not matched in the code; the dialog title and placeholder were found.
steps: Open Projects from the sidebar and click Create project.
Click into the Project name box.
Type a name and check the box has a visible label or placeholder.
Click elsewhere and check the box is still announced with its name.

S8.10.note: The placeholder is a default value (ChatComposerNew.tsx:811) and may be replaced by a page placeholder.
steps: Open a chat and click into the message box.
Type a first line, press Return, type a second line.
Check the box keeps both lines and grows in height.
Note which key adds a new line and which key sends the message; the code did not confirm the newline key.
S8.10.where: Chat > the message box at the bottom (placeholder Ask anything. Type / for commands)

S8.11.note: The search box has aria-label Search models (ModelCatalogue.tsx:640). Another search box, Search library files, sits in ComposerFilesMenu.tsx; its entry point was not confirmed.
steps: Open a chat and click the model name to open the Models picker.
Click into the Search models box.
Type a model name and check the list filters as you type.
Clear the box and check the full list comes back.
S8.11.where: Chat > the model name at the bottom of the composer (Models picker) > Search models

S8.12.needs: a connector that uses an API key
S8.12.note: The form is a password-type input (ConnectorApiKeyForm.tsx:194). Whether it opens from Settings or the workspace Connectors page was not confirmed.
steps: Open Connectors and pick a connector that takes an API key.
Click Add API key.
Type a value into the API key box.
Check the text is hidden as dots (masked) instead of shown in clear text.
S8.12.where: Connectors > pick a connector that uses an API key > Add API key

S8.13.needs: an email inbox that receives the sign-in code
S8.13.note: The code screen has other headings (Verify this device, Confirm your email) for other cases; the sign-in steps before this screen were not traced.
steps: Start sign-in with an email address and click Continue.
On the Check your inbox screen, look for the code box.
Paste or type the numeric code from the email.
Check the box accepts numbers and offers one-time-code autofill where the browser supports it.
S8.13.where: Sign-in > enter your email > Continue > Check your inbox (code box)

S8.14.note: The checkbox is in EnhancedExportDialog.tsx and mounted from WebChatPage.tsx:7934, but the menu item that opens the export dialog was not found, so the path is unverified. Searched for the dialog's trigger in the chat title menu.

labels.text: What do you want to do first?

S8.15.needs: a new account that has not finished onboarding
S8.15.note: Option labels are in use-cases.ts: Write and debug code, Write and edit, Research and analyze, Get things done at work, Learn something new.
steps: Start a new account or one that has not finished onboarding.
On Step 1 type a name and continue.
On Step 2, read the question What do you want to do first? and pick one option.
Check only one option is selected at a time and the selected one shows as checked.
S8.15.where: First sign-in onboarding > Step 2 of 2 > What do you want to do first?

S8.16.needs: a model that supports extended thinking
S8.16.note: The switch shows only when showThinkingSwitch is true (ComposerFooter.tsx:1910-1916).
steps: Choose a model that supports extended thinking and open the Effort button next to the model name.
Find the row labelled Effort with a switch.
Click the switch and see it turn on or off immediately.
Check that the switch state matches the Effort button text (Off or the effort name).
S8.16.where: Chat > the Effort button next to the model name in the composer > the Effort row switch (aria-label Toggle extended thinking)

S8.17.note: The control shows icons only; the words are aria-labels (CodeRail.tsx:379, 384). Desktop styles apply to it too (CloudCodePage.module.css:80).
steps: Open the Code area from the app.
Look at the top row of the left rail for the two-part control.
Hover each part; the current one (Code) is marked as the current page.
Click the Go to chat part and check it opens chat.
S8.17.where: Code > top of the left rail: the two-part icon control (Code and Go to chat)

S8.18.needs: a conversation with several messages from you and the assistant
S8.18.note: The filter panel shows only when canFilterConversations is true (GlobalSearchDialog.tsx:556). The toggle button's visible text was not found.
steps: Open the search dialog from the app.
Open the filter panel using its toggle (the toggle has no visible text in code).
Click the Message Type box and pick each option: All messages, My messages, AI responses, System messages.
Check the list of results changes to match the chosen type.
S8.18.where: Search (the search dialog) > filter toggle > Message Type

S8.19.note: Cmd+K is the shortcut in CommandPaletteProvider.tsx:16. The model submenu uses a Filter models… box instead.
steps: Press Cmd+K.
Type part of a chat title or an action name into the box.
Use the arrow keys to move through the list and press Return to pick one.
Check the list filters as you type and the highlighted item is the one picked.
S8.19.where: Press Cmd+K (command palette) > Search chats and actions

S8.20.note: These are checkbox items, not removable chips. This is the closest match to a multiselect in the code, so the match is weak.
steps: Open Code and open the Changes panel.
Click the More button (...).
Tick or untick Terminal and Exit codes (if shown) under Changes settings.
Check each choice shows as checked or unchecked, and the panel changes to match.
S8.20.where: Code > Changes panel > the More button (...) > Changes settings > Terminal

S8.21.note: The chip input is ChipInput.tsx and is also used for other lists (Approved hosts). The remove control's label is Remove {entry} from the allow list.
steps: Sign in as a workspace admin and open the Policy page in the workspace console.
Find the IP allow list section.
Type an address or block such as 203.0.113.0/24 and press Return or type a comma.
Check the entry becomes a removable chip, and click its remove control to check it is removed.
S8.21.where: Workspace console > Policy > IP allow list

S8.22.note: The field appears only for the interval recurrence; the exact condition (around ScheduleForm.tsx:338) was not confirmed. Arrow buttons depend on the browser's native number control.
steps: Open Scheduled from the sidebar and click New task.
Find the Repeat Every box with an interval recurrence.
Click the box and use the up and down arrows or type a number.
Check the value changes by one per step and cannot go below 1.

S8.23.needs: a model that has several effort levels
S8.23.note: The slider shows only when the model has several effort levels (ComposerFooter.tsx:1883-1950).
steps: Choose a model that offers several effort levels and open the Effort button beside the model name.
Drag the slider or press the left and right arrow keys.
Check the selected level label updates as the slider moves.
Compare the label with the Effort row text.
S8.23.where: Chat > the Effort button next to the model name in the composer > Effort slider

S8.25.needs: a conversation with messages on several dates
S8.25.note: The filter toggle's visible text was not found in code, same as S8.18.
steps: Open the search dialog and open its filter panel.
Click the From Date button labelled Select date.
Pick a day in the calendar that opens.
Check the button shows the chosen date in the format Month day, year.
S8.25.where: Search (the search dialog) > filter toggle > From Date > Select date

S8.26.note: The field is a native time input (ScheduleForm.tsx:391); it is shown only for daily, weekly and monthly recurrences.
steps: Open Scheduled and click New task.
Choose a recurrence of daily, weekly or monthly.
Click the Local Time field and set a time.
Check the field shows the chosen time in the browser's native time control.

S8.27.note: The suggestions come from a native datalist of Intl time zones (ScheduleForm.tsx:514-527); the default comes from schedule-form.ts:77.
steps: Open Scheduled and click New task.
Check the Time Zone box already holds your device zone (the code uses the browser's zone, with UTC as fallback).
Click the box, type a city or region such as Lon and pick a suggestion.
Check the suggestion list is searchable and the chosen zone stays in the box.

S8.28.needs: a project to open (a Free account can create one)
S8.28.note: The code shows the Colour section on the project page; I did not confirm the menu path that leads to a project.
steps: Open the Projects page and open one of your projects.
Find the section headed Colour.
Click one of the colour circles and check that the project's colour changes.
Click the dashed circle labelled Custom colour, pick a colour, and check that the chosen colour is used.

S8.29.note: The label of the button that opens this menu was not found in the code; the hidden file input has the accessible name File upload.
steps: Open a new chat.
Click the files button in the message box (its exact label was not found in the code).
Click Upload from device.
Choose a file in the system file picker and check that the file appears as an attachment in the message box.
S8.29.where: Chat composer > files button > Upload from device

S8.30.note: The overlay in apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/DragDropOverlay.tsx has no visible words in the code I read, so there is no label to search for.
steps: Open a chat in the browser or desktop app.
Drag a file from Finder over the window and hold it there.
Check that a full-screen overlay with a dimmed background appears while the file is over the window.
Drop the file and check that it is added as an attachment.
S8.30.where: Chat > drag a file from Finder over the app window

S8.31.note: ResearchPanel has a tablist labelled Research views with a Sources tab; I did not find how a person opens the research panel, and the second tab's label was not captured.

S8.32.note: Steps is the accessible name of the list, not a visible heading I could confirm; the trigger prompt is inferred from the parser.
steps: Ask the assistant for a step-by-step plan so that a steps card appears in the reply.
Look at the list of steps inside the card; the first step should be open.
Click another step row and check that it opens while the previous one closes.
Click the circle beside a step and check that the progress count changes.
S8.32.where: Chat > a reply that shows a numbered list of steps > steps card

S8.33.needs: a model that returns thinking steps
S8.33.note: The label is an accessible name for an icon button; I did not find visible text for it.
steps: Send a message to a model that returns thinking steps.
Find the small button with a brain icon under the reply.
Click it and check that the thinking steps appear, with the chevron turning down.
Click it again and check that the steps hide.
S8.33.where: Chat > a reply that has thinking steps > thinking toggle under the reply

S8.34.note: The button's accessible name is Conversation options; the title's exact visible position was not checked. Add chat instructions is shown only when the edit action is available.
steps: Open a conversation.
Click the conversation title at the top.
Check that a menu opens with Rename and Add chat instructions (or Edit chat instructions).
Press Escape or click outside and check that the menu closes.
S8.34.where: Chat > title at the top of the conversation (the button with a down arrow) > menu

S8.36.note: Move to project is shown only when projects exist; once the chat is in a project it reads Change project.
steps: Open a conversation while you have at least one project.
Click the conversation title, then choose Move to project.
Check that a sub-menu opens with the list of projects.
Hover or press the arrow key on the item, then check that the sub-menu opens.
S8.36.where: Chat > title at the top of the conversation > Move to project

S8.37.note: The pencil button only appears when the edit action is available for that message; I did not confirm the exact condition.
steps: Open a conversation that has a sent message.
Hover over the pencil icon under the message.
Check that a small label Edit appears above it.
Move the pointer away and check that the label disappears.
S8.37.where: Chat > hover over the pencil icon under your message

S8.38.note: The trigger label is not found; the menu's search and the Escape behaviour were not checked in the code.
steps: Open a new chat.
Click the files button in the message box (its label was not found in the code).
Check that a floating menu opens above the box with a search field and Upload from device.
Press Escape, then check that the menu closes; click the outside of the menu and check it closes too.

S8.39.note: A citation chip component exists in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/CitationChip.tsx, but I did not read its hover-card content, so I cannot say which visible words a person sees.

S8.40.note: The badge shows the unit text from the calculation; its visible text is data-driven, so no fixed label exists in the code.
steps: Ask the assistant for a calculation that has a unit, such as a measurement.
Look at the result card under the large result number.
Check that the unit appears as a small grey badge beside the result.
Compare with the result card's Copy result button to confirm the card layout.
S8.40.where: Chat > ask for a calculation > result card > unit badge

S8.41.note: The calculation card uses the same Badge component for units; I did not find a separate tag component that is distinct from status badges.

S8.42.note: I did not find a visible avatar or author marker in apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/MessageBubble.tsx; the line cited is a step-number circle. The unified-chat MessageBubble lines cited were not read.

S8.43.note: The percentage text is built from a template, so only the completion message is a fixed visible string.
steps: Open a reply that shows a steps card.
Look at the progress line at the top, which shows a count such as 0/3 and a percentage.
Click the circle beside each step to complete it.
Check that the count and percentage go up, and that All steps completed! appears when every step is done.
S8.43.where: Chat > reply with a numbered step list > progress line at the top of the steps card

S8.44.note: Loading chat is the accessible name of the placeholder; it is not visible text.
steps: Open an existing conversation, or reload the page with a slow connection.
Watch the area where messages will appear.
Check that grey placeholder bars stand in for messages before the real messages appear.
Compare what replaces the placeholders with what you saw before loading.
S8.44.where: Chat > open an existing conversation > loading placeholder

labels.text: Could not save the model for this conversation. The previous model remains active.

S8.45.needs: a conversation whose model change fails to save
S8.45.note: The toast text is in ComposerFooter.tsx, but I did not find a normal way to make the save fail, and I did not check how the toast dismisses itself.

S8.46.note: Inline alert blocks exist in the chat page (a role alert banner in apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx) and a status notice in MessageBubble, but I did not read the visible words of these blocks, so I cannot name one.

labels.text: Get notified when the response is ready.

S8.47.note: The banner shows only when the notification banner condition is true; that condition was not checked.
steps: Send a message that generates a long response.
Look at the strip under the header; it should say Get notified when the response is ready.
Click Enable and check the browser's permission prompt appears.
Click the close button on the strip and check that it goes away.
S8.47.where: Chat > send a message that takes a long time > banner at the top

S8.48.needs: more projects than fit on one page
S8.48.note: The Show more button appears only when there are more projects to load.
steps: Open the Projects page with more projects than one page holds.
Scroll to the bottom of the list.
Click Show more and watch the spinner and the Loading projects text.
Check that more projects are added to the list.
S8.48.where: Projects > scroll to the bottom of the list > Show more

S8.49.note: I did not confirm how the Artifacts panel is opened.
steps: Open the Artifacts panel in a chat with no generated files.
Check that the title No artifacts yet appears.
Read the description under it and compare it with what you expected.
Create a file or code artifact and check that the empty state goes away.
S8.49.where: Artifacts panel with no artifacts yet > No artifacts yet

S8.50.needs: a way to make the request fail (such as turning off the network)
S8.50.note: The Try again button belongs to the chat failure notice, which shows when a conversation fails to render; the Retry button is on the projects page. The error text for the projects page was not captured.
steps: Make the projects list fail to load, for example by going offline.
Check that an error message appears in place of the list.
Click Retry.
Check that the list loads when the connection comes back.
S8.50.where: Projects > if the projects list fails to load > Retry
